subject: 62A8DB017E8EEB11B3A3991393795E72
introduction: “Strengthen, O my God, my limbs and my heart and my tongue for Thy service.” These prayers ask one thing in many ways: to be made useful. They ask for bodily strength, for a collected mind, for the removal of whatever hinders, and above all for “servitude”, the station ‘Abdu’l-Bahá claimed for himself in his name. Isaiah’s “Here am I; send me”, the washing of the disciples’ feet, and “the least of these my brethren” are the Gospel’s account of service; Herbert’s servant sweeping a room and Milton’s “they also serve who only stand and wait” are two English poets on what counts as serving.
questions: Why pray to be able to serve, when one could simply begin?
What do these prayers treat as the obstacles to service?
Milton says those who wait also serve. Do the prayers leave room for that?

outside.why: I entertain no desire but this. Whom shall I send? Then said I, here am I; send me.
To serve Thy loved ones, gladden hearts and comfort. Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
Strengthen my limbs and my heart and my tongue for Thy service. Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.
Enable us to serve the world of humanity. By love serve one another.
Unite my scattered affairs, that I may serve. Unite my heart to fear thy name.
We are helpless; Thou art the Lord of strength. My strength is made perfect in weakness.
We are weak; strengthen us. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Lay thy head on the Threshold on my behalf. Ye also ought to wash one another’s feet.
Confirmed in servitude to Thy loved ones. Whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister.

This servant hopeth for Thy favours. When ye shall have done all, say, we are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do. Do these prayers expect a reward for service, and should they?
Aid me to serve Thee and Thy loved ones. Herbert: who sweeps a room as for Thy laws makes that and the action fine.
To aid me in service. Milton, blind and unable to do what he had hoped: they also serve who only stand and wait. Is there service in these prayers for someone who can do nothing?

shortfall: The remaining forty prayers repeat the request for confirmation in service; companions were set to the first fourteen readings.
